title.narrative: Sustainable enterprises create productive, green and decent jobs

description.narrative: Namibia continues to face persistent challenges related to high unemployment, low productivity, limited enterprise competitiveness and unequal access to sustainable economic opportunities, particularly affecting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), informal economy operators, rural communities and vulnerable groups, including youth. Enterprises in both the formal and informal economy face constraints such as limited access to finance, weak business development services, regulatory barriers, low levels of technological adoption and inadequate integration into value chains. At the same time, Namibia has significant potential for job creation and enterprise development in key growth sectors, including agriculture and agro-processing, fisheries, tourism, renewable energy, green hydrogen, manufacturing, digital services and the creative economy. Unlocking this potential requires targeted interventions to improve productivity, strengthen value chains and enhance the resilience and sustainability of enterprises. The ILO is extending support to strengthen the enabling environment for sustainable enterprises that generate productive, green and decent jobs. The intervention promotes enterprise competitiveness, productivity growth and responsible business conduct (RBC) across supply chains, ensuring that economic expansion is underpinned by respect for labour standards, environmental sustainability and social inclusion. It also supports improved access to business development services- including technical skills, financial inclusion and policies that foster decent work opportunities in both rural and urban economies. The ILO further supports the development and operationalization of policy and regulatory frameworks conducive to sustainable enterprise development, including measures that promote formalization of informal enterprises, youth entrepreneurship, productivity improvements and just transition pathways.
